knowledge_weighting.method: entry-weighted mean of O*NET 31.0 importance (Scale IM): entry targets weight 2; other linked occupations in Job Zone 4 or 5 (or the entry targets' Job Zone) weight 1; Manager, Chief, Postsecondary-faculty, All Other, Supervisor, Director and Treasurers and Controllers titles, and non-target occupations in other Job Zones, weight 0
knowledge_weighting.note: top_knowledge/top_skills are the unweighted mean over all linked occupations (kept for comparison); the outline uses the entry-weighted lists.

skipped_knowledge.reason: service and client-relations knowledge; the outline leaves it to internships, part-time work and the practice tasks rather than a course slot
management and planning knowledge matters most after several years of experience, so the outline gives it no course slot (a management elective is optional)

outline_elements.rule: English Language is placed in Year 1 general education; workplace and management elements (Customer and Personal Service, Administrative, Clerical, Administration and Management, Personnel and Human Resources, Education and Training) get no course slot unless the major's CIP series is about them; the next three elements go to Year 2 and up to three more (ordered by importance to the entry targets) to Year 3; if fewer than two remain for Year 3, knowledge rated at least 2.5 for the entry targets fills it

method.supervisory_tasks: task statement matches a supervisory/managerial pattern (supervise, provide supervision, direct and coordinate, direct the work/activities/staff of, manage staff/personnel/employees/workers/teams, oversee the work/staff, hire, subordinates, assign work to, evaluate the work/performance of, train and supervise); 'under supervision' does not count

quality_flags.note: Authored tier: entry targets and practice tasks were chosen and reviewed per major, so the generated-tier plausibility flags are not applied. Informational only: cited tasks whose O*NET statement is supervisory are listed; their authored scenarios say when they are practice for a later or graduate role.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Invented case: residents report muddy water flowing from a housing construction site into a creek after storms. As the environmental specialist for the county, write the investigation plan: what you review before the visit (the site's stormwater permit and erosion control plan), what you inspect on site (silt fences, inlet protection, stabilized entrances, sediment basins), samples or photos you collect and how, interviews, how you determine whether a violation occurred, and the documentation for possible enforcement.

rubric.description: Reviews the permit, plan and past inspection history before visiting.
Collects defensible evidence (dated photos, sampling with chain of custody, field notes) tied to permit requirements.
Links observations to specific permit conditions and documents findings for enforcement.

reference_answer_outline: Review permit coverage, erosion and sediment control plan, inspection logs.
Inspect controls and discharge points; photograph with GPS and time.
Turbidity samples upstream and downstream with chain of custody.
Interview site superintendent; request maintenance records.
Findings report referencing permit conditions and required corrective actions.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Invented data: you sampled dissolved oxygen, temperature, pH, conductivity and E. coli at four creek sites monthly for a year. Write the data report for the watershed council: how data were recorded and quality-checked (calibration logs, duplicates, holding times), a summary table, two charts you would include (with types and axes), comparison with the state water quality criteria (cite the source type), and plain-language findings with limitations.

rubric.description: Describes recording, calibration and QC checks and how flagged data were handled.
Tables and charts are appropriate, labeled and compare sites and seasons.
Compares with applicable criteria correctly and states limitations and next steps.

reference_answer_outline: Field sheets, meter calibration records, field duplicates, E. coli holding time compliance.
Table of seasonal medians by site.
Charts: time series of dissolved oxygen by site; bar chart of E. coli geometric mean.
Criteria from the state water quality standards; exceedances noted.
Findings: downstream site lower oxygen in summer; recommend source investigation.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Invented case: a small furniture-finishing shop applies for a minor-source air permit, reporting that it uses 3,000 liters of solvent-based coatings a year. Write the review: the information you check for completeness, how you estimate emissions from coating usage and solvent content (show the calculation with labeled assumptions), whether the shop's estimate qualifies it for the requested permit type, missing records you would request, and the decision memo.

rubric.description: Checks required application elements and supporting records (safety data sheets, purchase records).
Emission estimate uses volume, density and VOC content correctly with stated assumptions.
Decision memo ties conclusions to rules and identifies deficiencies or conditions.

reference_answer_outline: Checklist: facility information, process description, materials, controls, signatures.
Emission estimate: liters times density times VOC fraction gives kilograms per year.
Compare with the permit threshold in the applicable rules.
Request safety data sheets and 12 months of purchase records.
Memo: approve with recordkeeping conditions or request more information.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A state highway widening will fill 0.8 hectares of wetland and cross a trout stream; the permit requires monitoring during construction and for five years afterward. Write the monitoring plan: indicators (turbidity, temperature, macroinvertebrates, wetland vegetation, hydrology at the mitigation site), locations and frequency, methods and quality control, thresholds that trigger corrective action, and annual reporting.

rubric.description: Indicators match the impacts and permit conditions.
Uses control and impact sites, before and after data, and appropriate frequency.
Defines thresholds and corrective actions and a reporting schedule.

reference_answer_outline: Before-after-control-impact design with upstream reference site.
Continuous turbidity and temperature during construction; macroinvertebrates spring and fall.
Mitigation wetland: vegetation cover, invasive species, groundwater levels.
Thresholds: turbidity over background triggers inspection and stopping work; low native cover triggers replanting.
Annual reports to the permitting agency.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Invented case: a family's private well test shows nitrate at a level above the federal drinking water standard for public systems and detects total coliform bacteria. The parents have a 3-month-old baby. Write the phone conversation script and follow-up letter: how you explain the results clearly without alarming or minimizing, immediate precautions (especially for infant formula), what the coliform result may mean, retesting and treatment options, and where they can get further help.

rubric.description: Explains results and standards correctly in plain language.
Prioritizes the infant's safety with correct precautions (do not boil water for nitrate; use an alternative source for formula).
Gives retesting, treatment options and referrals to health department or certified contractors.

reference_answer_outline: Result explanation with units and the standard as a comparison.
Nitrate: boiling concentrates it; use bottled water for formula and drinking now.
Coliform: indicator of possible contamination; shock chlorination and retest.
Treatment options for nitrate such as reverse osmosis or ion exchange; well inspection.
Letter with results, advice, contacts and retest date.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Continuing the construction runoff case, the inspection confirmed failed silt fences and sediment reaching the creek. Write the notice of violation letter and a plan for the conversation with the site manager: the facts and the permit conditions violated, required corrective actions with deadlines, potential penalties under the applicable rules (refer to the rule type without inventing amounts), the right to respond, and how you keep the tone firm but professional.

rubric.description: Notice cites dates, observations, evidence and exact permit conditions.
Corrective actions and deadlines are specific and verifiable.
Explains penalties and rights accurately, keeps a professional tone and documents the conversation.

reference_answer_outline: Heading, permit number, inspection date and observations with photo references.
Conditions violated, quoted by number from the permit.
Corrective actions: repair silt fence within 48 hours, stabilize slopes, clean creek sediment under guidance.
Penalty language referencing the enforcement rules; right to respond within a set period.
Conversation: firm facts, listen, agree on reinspection date, written follow-up.
